sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: runFilter()'s in-place single-table filter path (PERFORMANCE.org Step 1) never re-synced a collapsed multi-row cell's mb-collapse-toggle-has-match indicator after applying a NEW filter's highlight, because initCollapsableColumns() — the only place that used to stamp that class — now runs once at initial render instead of after every filter pass. A match landing inside an already-built, already-collapsed cell (e.g. selecting a 'Join phrases' value like 'Featuring' that only matches a hidden <li>) showed no red/yellow 'hidden match' cue until the user manually expanded and re-collapsed that specific cell, which recomputes has-match via a separate, correct code path (ensureCollapseDelegate's click handler). Fixed by calling the existing _syncCollapseHasMatchInTable() helper (already used by applySubFilter() for the identical sub-table-filter case) right after the in-place show/hide pass, alongside the CAA/EAA bigbox sync that already runs there for the same 'used to happen via the old per-pass rebuild, now needs an explicit call' reason. The multi-table path (renderGroupedTable(), which still calls initCollapsableColumns() per sub-table on every filter pass) was unaffected.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: PERFORMANCE.org Step 7 (decouple IDB caching from the icon-render hot path): a CAA/EAA icon cache MISS (sa_art_idb_enable=true) no longer blocks its visible background-image paint on a full GM_xmlhttpRequest→Blob→createObjectURL round-trip. _artLoadIcon now checks the local memory/IndexedDB cache tiers only (new _artCheckLocalCache, still fast/local, unchanged for actual hits); on a miss it displays the icon immediately via the same native request path used when IDB is disabled (factored into a shared _artLoadNativeImg(ctx, imgurl, onSuccess, onError) helper), while a new, separately-queued background task (_artBackgroundCacheToIdb, on a new low-concurrency _caaBgCacheQueue — default 4, new sa_art_idb_bg_cache_concurrency setting) fetches the same image and writes it to IndexedDB purely so a future page load gets a fast IDB hit. Investigating the original 'jesus2099 assigns img.src immediately' premise (from PERFORMANCE.org's Step 6 WIP.6 entry) against debug/jesus-coverart.js directly found it inaccurate — that script's own icon loader also gates its visible paint on img.onload, it just never has an IDB/blob step in front of it; the real fix is removing that extra hop, not removing a blocking wait that both approaches always had. _artFetchCachedImage (still used by hover preview, the big-picture strip, and inline thumbnails) is untouched — _artBackgroundCacheToIdb reuses it as a thin wrapper rather than duplicating its fetch+IDB-write logic, avoiding any regression risk to those unrelated callers. The per-icon cache-hint badge and _caaFetchStats toast counters are unchanged by design (per explicit choice): a miss-then-native-display icon now lands in the existing 'browser' telemetry bucket instead of the old synthetic 'network' bucket, which is more accurate, not a regression. Both existing icon retry mechanisms (per-icon ⚠⟳, per-table 'Retry' button) already forced cacheBust=true and were already using this native-fallback code path — unaffected, just now routed through the shared helper instead of a duplicated inline block.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: PERFORMANCE.org Step 5 follow-up: fixed a visible stall on large lazy-loaded tables (sa_caa_io_threshold, e.g. an 800-row series/events page) where dragging the scrollbar quickly to a distant part of the table showed only the header row for a moment before rows appeared — a scroll-jank/checkerboard symptom, not missing row data (all rows are fully built at initial render, unchanged since before Step 5). Root cause: a fast scrollbar-drag jump brings dozens/hundreds of off-screen icons within the IntersectionObserver's 200px root margin at once, and the callback previously ran that whole batch's unobserve+enqueue work synchronously in a single task, competing with the browser for the main thread it needed to paint the just-scrolled-to rows — a collision that couldn't happen before Step 5, since all artwork loaded once at initial render, before the user had started scrolling. Fixed with a new _artProcessIoEntriesBatched(), which splits the callback's intersecting entries into 20-entry chunks (_ART_IO_BATCH_SIZE) and processes one chunk per requestAnimationFrame instead of the whole burst in one tick; _artInitLazyPics()'s observer callback now delegates to it. Does not change Step 6's request-concurrency queues — only spreads the DOM-mutation cost of starting observer-triggered loads/enrichment across frames.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: PERFORMANCE.org Step 6 (CAA/EAA request-throughput tuning): the single shared _caaQueue (concurrency 4, sa_caa_fetch_concurrency) is split into two independent queues — _caaImgQueue for image loads (icon thumbnails, inline thumbnails, big-picture strip) and _caaMetaQueue for _artEnrichIcon's JSON count-lookup fetch() calls. Investigating why debug/jesus-coverart.js (jesus2099's mb_FUNKEY-ILLUSTRATED-RECORDS, the script this feature was originally modeled on) loads inline cover art dramatically faster found that its unthrottled requests never hit a CORS/rate-limit wall because native loads (and its GM_xmlhttpRequest-equivalent unthrottled XHR) are never CORS-bound in the first place — CORS only gates script code reading response bytes (fetch()/XHR body, canvas pixels), not the browser displaying an image. Our own image paths (_artLoadIcon's GM_xmlhttpRequest CORS-bypass fetch, and its native fallback) are equally CORS-free, yet were sharing the same 4-slot budget as _artEnrichIcon's fetch() JSON calls — the one CAA/EAA request path that IS CORS-sensitive. New settings sa_caa_img_concurrency (default 12, was 4) and sa_caa_meta_concurrency (default 6) replace sa_caa_fetch_concurrency; _artInitQueue() now creates and cancels both queues each render pass, and a new _caaQueuesOnIdle() helper fires the completion toast once both queues (rather than one shared queue) have drained. All 10 former _caaQueue.enqueue() call sites were reclassified by request kind: 8 image-load sites (ergInjectCaaInlineThumbnails, _artLoadIcon's retry handler, _artInitLazyPics's icon branch, _artInitSmallPics, _loadBigImgIdb/_loadBigImg, the inline-pics refetch task, init{CAA,EAA}InlinePics's loadTask) now enqueue on _caaImgQueue; the 2 _artEnrichIcon sites (_artInitLazyPics's enrichment branch, _artEnrichTable) now enqueue on _caaMetaQueue. No behavior change to WHEN requests fire (PERFORMANCE.org Step 5's IntersectionObserver lazy-loading and sa_caa_io_threshold are untouched) — only how many of each kind can run concurrently. A more invasive follow-up idea surfaced during this investigation — rendering icons immediately via the plain URL like jesus2099's script, with GM_xmlhttpRequest→Blob→IndexedDB persistence moved to a background-only step instead of gating the visible render — is documented as PERFORMANCE.org Step 7 (not yet implemented).

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: PERFORMANCE.org Step 5 (lazy CAA/EAA loading via IntersectionObserver): for tables at or above a new sa_caa_io_threshold setting (default 500 data rows), CAA/EAA icon background-image loads and JSON-API enrichment are deferred until each artwork-icon cell scrolls within 200px of the viewport, instead of firing for every row at initial render. A persistent per-archive IntersectionObserver (_caaArtIO / _eaaArtIO) is created once by the new _artInitLazyPics() and observes every icon in the table; on intersect it unobserves the element and enqueues the same _artLoadIcon()/_artEnrichIcon() calls the eager path already used, through the shared _caaQueue. The observer survives filter/sort passes since WIP.1 keeps allRows as live DOM rows and initCaaPics()/initEaaPics() now run once per render instead of per keystroke; _artInitQueue() (the shared once-per-render-pass reset point already used for _caaQueue) now also disconnects and nulls any previous _caaArtIO/_eaaArtIO so a fresh render observes the current DOM set. Below the threshold, when IntersectionObserver is unavailable, or when the setting is 0, both paths run eagerly exactly as before. Reimplemented from archive/filter-performance-fix-v1-single-table's WIP.2 ("Pattern 5") against current main; the big-picture strip above the table (_artInitBigPics) is unaffected — only the per-row icon column and its enrichment are deferred, matching the archived branch's scope.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: PERFORMANCE.org Step 4 (openUniqDrop() per-open caching): the unique-values dropdown's 5 full tbody.rows scan passes (whole-cell value counts, flag-icon segment map, relationship-cell detection, relationship icon counts, inline CAA/EAA-thumbnail counts) now share Step 3's exact caching primitive — a per-(table, column) WeakMap cache keyed by a signature of the currently visible rows' data-mb-row-idx values, via a new shared _visibleRowSetSignature() (factored out of _updateAllColHeaderCounts's own inline loop, which now calls it too instead of duplicating the loop). Reopening the same column's dropdown with no filter/sort change in between skips straight past all 5 passes. Found and fixed one correctness gap while implementing: the "Cell structure" section's collapsed/expanded split is read from expandedCells (individually-toggled cells), not derivable from the visible-row signature, so a lone cell expand/collapse click would otherwise leave a reopened dropdown showing a stale split. Added _invalidateUniqDropDataCache(table, colIndex) and wired it into all 5 places expandedCells is mutated by user interaction (_applyCollapseState()'s two branches, ensureCollapseDelegate()'s three inline toggle branches).

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: PERFORMANCE.org Step 3 (cache _updateAllColHeaderCounts): the per-column unique-value/multi-row header-count scan (O(rows x columns), the file's own documented worst case) now memoizes its result per <table> against a cheap O(rows) signature of the currently visible rows' data-mb-row-idx values, and skips the full recompute whenever that signature is unchanged since the last call. This makes syncCollapseButtonsWithColumnVisibility's column show/hide re-init (:16555) and multi-table sub-table re-renders (:42643, :43189) free when the visible row set hasn't actually changed. The one known call site that mutates cell CONTENT in place without changing which rows are visible — initReleaseEventsColumn()'s two post-population re-scans of initCollapsableColumns() (:52605, :52616), which fill previously-empty Release events/country/date cells — now explicitly calls the new _invalidateColHeaderCountsCache() first so those counts still refresh correctly instead of reading stale (pre-population) cached values.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: PERFORMANCE.org Step 2 (extend Fix C to Sort, single-table mode): applyMultiSortColumnTints() now skips filter-hidden rows when computing shade-toggle boundaries, so tint bands reflect only the visible rows again — after WIP.1 the tbody permanently holds the full row set (hidden rows kept as display:none instead of removed), which previously let hidden rows shift the tint boundaries. The CAA/EAA big-picture strip's image order no longer freezes at its original fetch-time order after a sort: WIP.1 stopped calling initCaaPics()/initEaaPics() on every action, which used to rebuild the strip (and incidentally re-sort it) on every filter/sort pass; a new _artReorderBigBoxForTable() (plus caaReorderBigBoxForTable()/eaaReorderBigBoxForTable() wrappers) now cheaply moves the existing wrapper elements to match the table's new row order via box.appendChild — no rebuild, called once per sort from the sort handler right after it reorders the live tbody rows. The single-table sort path's own live-DOM-reorder (rows moved to match the new sort order before runFilter()'s show/hide pass runs, including the cdtoc tracklist sub-row fix) had already landed as part of WIP.1.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: PERFORMANCE.org Step 1 (filter re-render, single-table mode): runFilter() no longer clones matching rows, replaces the tbody, or re-runs the post-render hook chain (initCollapsableColumns and the CAA/EAA/ERG/CDtoc it drives, plus Picard rewiring) on every keystroke. allRows are now kept as the live DOM rows throughout the session; each filter pass strips stale highlight spans and applies display:none / display:'' directly on those rows, then syncs the CAA/EAA bigbox via the existing caaUpdateBigBoxForTable()/eaaUpdateBigBoxForTable() helpers (previously only used by sub-table filters). The hook chain now runs exactly once — already true for the live fetch pipeline (startFetchingProcess), and newly hoisted into the disk-load/hydration path (initCollapsableColumns moved after updateH2Count() so its global toggle button can find filterContainer already attached; initCaaPics/initEaaPics/initCaaInlinePics/initEaaInlinePics called directly there since runFilter() no longer initialises them for single-table mode). Sort reorders the live tbody rows in place (appendChild loop) before the show/hide filter pass runs, so visible rows stay in sorted order. Fixed a regression the show/hide approach would otherwise introduce for cdtoc pages: a filtered-out or re-sorted row's tracklist sub-row (a synthetic sibling <tr> from _cdtocInitTracklistToggles(), not part of allRows) is now hidden/moved alongside its parent row instead of being orphaned.
